description: Mars Survival Sidhas is a team exploring how astronauts can survive on Mars by combining NASA science with ancient sidhas wisdom. We focus on discipline, endurance, and creative storytelling to design a survival guide that blends culture and space exploration
summary: Project Mars Survival Sidhas is an interactive Mars exploration and survival platform designed to help future astronauts navigate the Martian surface safely and efficiently. The project brings together terrain information, environmental data, exploration routes, and hazard awareness into a single easy to use map. By integrating important Mars mission data, users can identify safer travel paths, locate scientifically interesting areas, and improve mission planning. Our solution supports future human exploration of Mars by providing a practical survival and navigation guide that enhances safety, decision making, and scientific discovery during Mars missions.
details:
Mars Survival Sidhas is a prototype Martian exploration and navigation planner designed to help future explorers plan surface missions on Mars. The project focuses on the Mount Sharp region and presents terrain information, possible hazards, exploration destinations, and route that planning concepts in one easy to understand interface.

The project works by guiding the user through a mission-planning process. The explorer selects an exploration area, reviews terrain and potential obstacles, considers a route between an astronaut base and a scientific exploration site, and reviews information that can support mission planning.

The goal of Mars Survival Sidhas is to make Mars surface exploration information easier to understand and bring important mission planning information together in one place. The prototype demonstrates how future versions could combine multiple NASA data layers and develop into a more interactive navigation system for Mars exploration.

The current version is a conceptual prototype rather than an operational navigation system. It demonstrates the proposed user experience, mission planning workflow, terrain assessment, and route-planning concept.
